subject: POC timeline, success criteria & next steps (post-demo)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Mendez <lisa.m@cirrusdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 16:24:00 -0800
Subject: POC timeline, success criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Hi Lisa — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC schedule and responsibilities.

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: Validate that Redwood reduces inference latency and per-token cost for CirrusSearch query enrichment without changing upstream infra.
- Success signals:
  - Latency: 95th percentile for enrichment calls under 250ms at expected QPS (baseline workload to be provided).
  - Cost: < 30% increase vs current CPU-based baseline on equivalent SLA, or clear cost-per-query improvement target depending on model choice.
  - Functional: Correctness > 95% on the 200-case prompt set you shared; no major hallucination cases in top-10 queries.
  - Operational: Private-data isolation for test indices, request-level audit logs enabled.

Proposed POC cadence (draft)
- Kickoff (remote): week of Dec 14 — 60–90 minute alignment meeting (owners, environment access, test datasets).
- Week 1 (Dec 15–21): Provisioning + baseline capture (Logan owner).
- Week 2 (Dec 22–28): Model selection, quantization candidates, and integration test (Marissa owner).
- Midpoint review (end of week 2): demo of baseline vs Redwood pilot results, decide go/no-go on scale tests.
- Week 3–4 (Jan 4–Jan 21): Scale runs, load testing, and reliability checks (Neha owner).
- Final readout / decision ceremony (week of Jan 25): acceptance by joint stakeholders and next-steps (procurement/commit).

Owners (initial)
- Cirrus: Lisa M. (product), Rajiv P. (procurement/finance)
- Redwood: Karthik (engagement owner), Marissa (SE, integration), Logan (SRE / infra), Neha (trial ops)

Immediate asks
1) Can you confirm the preferred kickoff date between Dec 14–16? We suggested Dec 15 as a target.
2) Please confirm the test dataset delivery timeline and whether we should expect sanitized copies or tokenized extracts.
3) Loop in procurement contact (Rajiv) if there are PO or legal prerequisites before kickoff.

Attachments: Im preparing a short mutual action plan (will share as an attachment in follow-up) and a checklist for environment access.

If that looks right Ill send the mutual action plan and a DocuSign link for the standard POC SOW so procurement can review.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik — thanks for the thorough recap. This aligns well with our expectations. A few quick notes: 

- Kickoff: Dec 15 works for our team (afternoon PT preferred). Please lock a 60–90 minute slot and send calendar invites.
- Test data: We can provide a sanitized 3K query sample by EOD Dec 10. Rajiv will confirm whether any additional NDAs are required for the full dataset.
- Procurement: looping in Rajiv (cc). Rajiv — can you confirm Cirrus procurement timeline for a POC SOW and whether a PO will be needed before Jan 1?

One other ask: can you include a short list of required hostnames/ports and a minimum VM spec (cpu/mem/gpu) so our infra team can provision the lab ahead of kickoff?

Thanks — Lisa

Perfect — locking Dec 15 (we'll send invites for 2:30pm PT).

Attached: Redwood_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx (single-sheet M.A.P. with timelines, owners, acceptance gates) — this is a working doc we will iterate on during kickoff.

Quick answers to Lisa's infra ask:
- Hostnames/ports: we need outbound access to api.redwood.ai:443 and a single inbound ssh bastion at port 22 for initial provisioning.
- Minimum lab spec: 1 x A10g-equivalent GPU (or T4 for low-scale runs), 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM, 200GB disk for model cache.

Procurement note: DocuSign link for the POC SOW: https://app.docusign.com/secure/12345-POC-SOW — Rajiv, if youd like us to route to your Ariba/PO flow we can do that; otherwise the SOW covers the trial terms and data handling SLA.

Next steps I will take before kickoff:
- Share finalized MAP (attached) and a short checklist for credentials/access.
- Create a HubSpot deal record and share the link here for tracking: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/1249876

Onboarding note: We propose a lightweight decision ceremony at the final readout — 30 minutes with exec sponsors to review acceptance metrics and procurement next steps. Thoughts?

— Karthik

Thanks all — quick technical pre-reqs and the trial environment checklist attached.

High-level technical asks (we'll walk these at kickoff):
- Test dataset: sanitized CSV with columns [query_id, query_text, expected_top_3_answers]. 3K rows is ideal for baseline.
- API keys: a temp API key for Cirrus test account (we'll generate scopes-limited keys to avoid data bleed).
- Network: allow outbound 443 to api.redwood.ai; inbound SSH only from your bastion IPs during provisioning window.
- Data retention: by default we keep trial logs for 30 days unless you request otherwise; we can adjust retention TTL on request.
- Observability: we'll enable token-level cost and latency dashboard and share an early dashboard link within 48 hours of provisioning.

Attached: Trial-Environment-Checklist.pdf (includes hostnames, port list, minimum VM spec, sample config file).

If procurement requires any technical appendices attached to the SOW, tell Rajiv and we’ll create a short technical addendum.

See you all on Dec 15 (calendar invite to follow).

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
